what_changed: The reader now consumes Deep2::QuantTypeTable (src/deep2/QuantTypeTable.hpp) as the single authority for ggml type geometry instead of a parallel switch statement. That closed the 13,141-tensor validation gap entirely.

gap_before_vs_after.note: The 13,141 unknown tensors were every K-quant. I had deliberately refused to size them rather than guess, which was the right call: the canonical table records that two of those sizes were previously wrong.

independent_proof.check: For every file, sort tensors by absolute offset and verify that the last tensor ends within 32 bytes of end-of-file, and that no two tensors overlap.
independent_proof.result: All 56 files have tiling delta exactly 0 and zero overlaps.
independent_proof.why_it_matters: A wrong K-quant block size would shift every subsequent tensor and make the last range overrun the file. delta 0 across 16 architectures and 26,829 tensors independently confirms the geometry, separate from the table itself.

why_the_canonical_table_was_needed: The table itself records that Q8_K was previously 29 bytes and IQ1_S 34 bytes, and IQ4_NL was sized 132/256. All three are wrong; the correct values are 292, 50 and 18/32.
Q8_1 is 36 bytes per 32 elements, which is easy to get wrong by assuming Q8_0 plus an extra scale.
MXFP4 is type 39 at 32 elements and 17 bytes. It is a real format, not a placeholder, and is now recognised by name and sized. gptoss uses it for a large share of expert weights.
acknowledged_corrections: MXFP4 is treated as a recognised format with verified geometry, not as an invalid type. Decoding support and kernel readiness are separate questions the table tracks explicitly via kernelReady, which is false for MXFP4 today.

deepseek2 and deepseek4 do not share an execution plan in this work. The reader reports their geometry separately, and the taxonomy records their differences: deepseek2 has 64 experts with expert_weights_scale 1.0, deepseek4 has 256 experts with scale 1.5 plus indexer tensors that deepseek2 does not have.

dtype_handling_now.sized_exactly: every type the canonical table gives non-zero geometry for, which covers all 26,829 tensors present in this store
dtype_handling_now.fail_closed: removed and zero-geometry ids still yield nbytes 0, so readRaw refuses rather than guessing
dtype_handling_now.readF32: still decodes F32, F16 and BF16 only. Block-format decoding belongs to the kernel that owns the format; this certificate makes no claim that arbitrary tensors can be materialised.

what_this_still_does_not_establish: No model is executed. No logits, tokens, TPS or parity result for any of the 56 models.
Discoverable is not executable. No architecture block plan has been built; Deep2 can still run only deepseek2.
nbytes is now derivable for every present tensor, but reading a quantised tensor back as F32 still requires a dequant kernel.
next: P0: connect the reader to Deep2ExecutionIR so one descriptor chain carries GGML ids and block geometry, with no parallel assumptions.
P0: bind the existing deepseek2 executor to its actual staged GGUF, which is library__deepseek-coder-v2__16b.gguf, and run real prefill plus multi-token decode.
